body: You also need to use `is_editor_hint()`, otherwise the gizmo draws at runtime...
You could add a case for `EMISSION_SHAPE_POINTS` and `EMISSION_SHAPE_DIRECTED_POINTS` too, it's not difficult.

Not needed, moving the node will move the gizmo together with it.
Unless it serves some purpose?
Could you clarify this a bit? The points are written to an array style texture which I'm not sure how to display effectively every frame.

In CPU Particles the emission points are a simple array of vectors.
For GPU Particles it's more complicated, yeah.

Also gizmo redrawing does not happen every frame (or at least it shouldn't).
I moved over to only showing the gizmos while selected, same as the visibility rect on GPUParticles.
As far as I can tell this is needed as the rendered gizmo does not follow CPU particles when local_coords is disabled.

I investigated adding this, but I don't think it makes sense. Even in the CPU particles, the points are a list of points that particles will randomly spawn at, not points that make up a shape that particles will spawn within. I don't see a nice way of rendering hundreds of points in the gizmo rendering that is readable for the user.
Then it should be called only in that case.
This method could be moved to `Particles2DEditorPlugin`, to avoid code duplication.
The new condition part is relevant only for editor.
Ehhh, not sure what I was thinking here. Thanks for catching that. Fixed.
Could the color be saved somewhere in a variable since it seems to be used a lot in several places?
set_show_gizmos only gets called by the particles_editor_plugin, so it already only runs in editor. So I don't believe that's needed.
